samples.summary: `format()`'s new throwing default branch escapes uncaught in `schema`, turning a bad `--format` into a raw Node stack trace
samples.evidence: formatter.ts:51-55 now throws `InvalidFormatError` from `format()` for any unrecognized `fmt`. Every other `output()` call site sits inside a try/catch that funnels to `outputError`, but `registerSchemaCommand` (schema.ts:26 and :33) calls `output(schema, opts.format, opts.quiet)` with no try/catch, and bin.ts:27 calls `program.parse()` with no top-level handler. So `wafflebase schema --format bogus` (or `--format md`, which the docs/slides/notes vocabularies make plausible) goes from printing `undefined` to an unhandled exception with a stack trace on stderr — exactly the unstructured failure this change set out to remove. The guard (`parseOutputFormat`) was added only to `status` and `ctx list`, so this path reaches the newly-throwing operation unprotected.

samples.summary: Throwing on unknown format inside `output()` makes mutating commands report exit 1 after the write already succeeded
samples.evidence: For every async command the format value is never validated before the request; `output(res.data, opts.format, opts.quiet)` is the first thing that sees it. With the new throw at formatter.ts:51-55, `cells set <doc> A1 5 --format bogus` (cells.ts:58-68) performs the PUT, then `output()` throws, the catch calls `outputError`, and the process exits 1 with `{"error":{"code":"INVALID_FORMAT"}}`. Nothing signals the mutation succeeded, so an agent branching on exit code will retry and double-apply the write. `parseOutputFormat` was placed before the work only in status/ctx.list; the mutating commands need the same up-front validation.

samples.summary: `--quiet` bypasses format validation for every command except the two changed here, giving inconsistent exit codes for the same bad flag
samples.evidence: `output()` returns at formatter.ts:60 before calling `format()` when quiet, so `tabs list --quiet --format bogus` never validates and exits 0. `status`/`ctx list` call `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` before `output()` (status.ts:64, ctx.ts:73), so the same flag combination exits 1 with no diagnostic. Identical invalid input yields different exit codes depending on the subcommand.

samples.summary: Comment claims the new structured error "matches `ctx switch`", but `ctx switch` still emits a plain-text message and `process.exit(1)`
samples.evidence: ctx.ts:75-78 says the logged-out error is structured "matching `ctx switch`". `ctx switch` at ctx.ts:92-97 does `console.error('Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.')` followed by `process.exit(1)` — unstructured text, no `code`, and a hard `process.exit` rather than `process.exitCode`. The two paths are not consistent, so an agent parsing stderr as JSON will fail on `ctx switch`.

samples.summary: `status --format csv` emits a different header row depending on login state
samples.evidence: `buildStatus` returns `{loggedIn, message}` when logged out and eight different keys when logged in (status.ts:33-56). `formatCsv` derives its header from `Object.keys(rows[0])` (csv.ts:13), so the CSV header is `loggedIn,message` in one state and `loggedIn,user,email,...` in the other — a consumer with a fixed column mapping mis-parses one of the two. The optional-field design (`message?`, `user?` …) makes the same shape instability visible in JSON too.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as described. `format()` now throws `InvalidFormatError` in its `default` branch (formatter.ts:51-55) and `output()` calls it unguarded (formatter.ts:59-62). The global `--format` option is declared with no `.choices()` validation (root.ts:53), so an arbitrary string flows into `opts.format`. `registerSchemaCommand` calls `output(...)` at schema.ts:26 and schema.ts:33 inside a synchronous action with no try/catch and no `outputError` funnel, unlike status.ts:64 and ctx.ts:73 which route through `parseOutputFormat` within guarded flows. `bin.ts:27` calls `program.parse()` with no top-level handler, and grep found no `exitOverride`, `configureOutput`, or `uncaughtException` hook in packages/cli/src. Therefore `wafflebase schema --format bogus` throws out of the commander action and surfaces as an uncaught exception with a raw stack trace rather than the structured INVALID_FORMAT error the change intends. Only mitigation found is the `quiet` short-circuit at formatter.ts:60, which does not cover the default (non-quiet) path. No named refutation ground applies; this is a real correctness/error-handling defect in the Correctness lane.

Real, reachable, unguarded, and in the Correctness lane (mis-reported failure / potential duplicate write); major impact.
